Choosing art as a personal gift: original, print or commission?

November 13, 2026

An art gift begins with the person receiving it: the images they return to, the rooms they live in and the amount of choice they would like to keep. Start there before choosing a size or price.

Let their taste guide the image

Notice what the recipient already lives with. Do they choose portraits, flowers, strong color or quieter scenes? You are looking for a connection rather than an exact match to furniture. Kimberly Marnell’s paintings bring figures, botanical forms and color into different relationships, so spend time with the individual work before choosing.

Queen of the Night offers a botanical portrait, while Golden Hour brings warm orange, pink and blue into a figurative composition. A recipient who enjoys those subjects may respond to either; the artwork page lets you compare medium, dimensions and availability.

Choose an original for a specific connection

An original is a unique physical artwork. That can make it a thoughtful gift when you know the recipient’s taste well, but the size and presentation deserve attention. Measure the space if you can do so appropriately. Confirm whether the work is framed, and allow for the cost and dimensions of a frame if it is not included.

Before buying, read the direct-original return policy. Change-of-mind returns are not offered for direct original artwork purchases. If the choice feels uncertain, ask Kimberly about the painting before you pay rather than assuming the recipient can exchange it later.

Choose a print for more flexibility in format

A print is a reproduction of an artwork, with its own size and material choices. It may suit a smaller wall or a different budget. The fine art print page links to the available marketplace routes. Check the live listing for current options and final checkout price; framing, shipping, tax and delivery estimates belong to that seller’s order process.

Check whether a gift should arrive framed or whether the recipient would prefer to choose that detail. A paper print’s image dimensions and paper dimensions can differ, so use the listing’s measurements when selecting a frame.

Choose a commission when the subject matters most

A personal painting can begin with a pet, a person, a place or an idea. A commission needs a conversation about references, size, medium, scope and timing. A birthday or holiday date is a request to discuss, not an automatic promise of delivery.

Prepare a few clear photographs that you own or have permission to use. Explain the connection you want the painting to hold and the date you have in mind. Start with the photo preparation guide, then use the commission form to plan the request.

Keep the practical details clear

Whether you choose an existing original, a print or a new commission, confirm the recipient’s available wall space, the framing plan and the delivery destination. Ask about timing before ordering for a particular occasion. The best starting point is the image they will enjoy returning to, supported by details you have checked.
